content: From a governance perspective, subsidiaries are typically structured to align with the overarching strategic goals, risk profiles, and operational priorities of the parent organization, necessitating clear mandates and communication channels to ensure efficiency and value creation [24] . From 2020 to 2023, the integration of AI into cybersecurity within the SaaS sector saw notable trends, aligning with the global trajectory of leveraging advanced technologies to combat evolving threats. Globally, artificial intelligence began transforming the cybersecurity landscape by substantially enhancing threat detection and response capabilities, automating mundane administrative tasks, and addressing highly sophisticated tactics, including AI-driven cyberattacks [33] [34] [35] . To mitigate these vulnerabilities, the integration of YAL.ai across Veramani’s subsidiary map heavily emphasized the implementation of Zero Trust architectures and real-time threat intelligence systems [33] . Although detailed historical data specific to South Africa’s advancements in AI-driven SaaS cybersecurity during the 2020 to 2023 period remains sparse, regional trends likely mirrored broader international developments. During this time, South Africa rapidly advanced its digital infrastructure and increased its reliance on SaaS ecosystems. The Threat Detection Efficiency across the holding company also exhibited an overall increasing trend during this period. Starting at a minimum value of 65.0% in 2020, the efficiency of threat detection systems climbed steadily in tandem with the integration efforts, reaching a maximum value of 97.0% in 2023. The implementation of artificial intelligence often presents distinct challenges, and valuable lessons can be drawn from broader industry examples regarding operational hurdles and the necessity of managing user experience and liability effectively [32] . Furthermore, the trajectory of responsible AI trends and operational applications forecasted for 2026 emphasizes the need for continuous oversight and ethical management of AI deployments [33] . For Veramani, ensuring that YAL.ai remains at the forefront of cybersecurity innovation involves navigating these implementation challenges while adhering to emerging frameworks for responsible AI usage. Looking toward the future, the cybersecurity landscape continues to evolve, driven by more intelligent and adaptive malware [34] .
